t: Kyoto began in 794 when Emperor Kanmu moved the court from Nara to Heian-kyō, a grid city modelled on Chang'an, and it remained the capital until the court moved to Tokyo in 1869.
Military rulers governed from Kamakura and Edo and, in the Muromachi period, from Kyoto itself, but the city stayed the seat of the emperors, and it was rebuilt after the Ōnin War of 1467–1477.
After the capital moved Kyoto built a canal, electric power and a modern municipality, and it was removed from the list of atomic bomb targets, so that much of its older building survives.
dyk: Japan's first electric tram line ran in Kyoto, made possible by the Lake Biwa Canal, which supplied hydroelectric power from 1895.
ev: The Shimogamo Shrine is believed to have been established in the area
Emperor Kanmu makes Heian-kyō the seat of the imperial court
The Ōnin War destroys much of the city
Toyotomi Hideyoshi rebuilds the streets and builds earthwork walls round the city

f.founded: Chosen in 794 by Emperor Kanmu as the new seat of the imperial court and laid out as Heian-kyō on the model of the Tang capital Chang'an; the Shimogamo Shrine is believed to date from the 6th century.
f.where: In the Yamashiro (Kyoto) Basin, ringed by hills on three sides, between the Kamo, Katsura and Uji rivers, on Honshu in the Kansai region of Japan.
f.known: Heian-kyō, the imperial capital from 794; the Ōnin War; the Muromachi shogunate; Hideyoshi's rebuilding of the streets; Nijō Castle; about 2,000 temples and shrines; kimono weaving; the Gion Matsuri
f.today: Kyoto is the capital of Kyoto Prefecture in the Kansai region, with about one and a half million people.
